title: Week 2
coldOpen: Six playoff spots. Twelve owners. Roughly ten legitimate plans to get there and two guys who are at least being honest with themselves. Welcome to the return of the PDL Power Rankings, preseason edition.

1: I spent all offseason correcting people when they called me pessimistic about Delco.
Realistic.
I said realistic.
Week 1 did a pretty good job making that distinction pointless.
Greg beat me 146.30 to 128.58, six days after I picked London to win the PDL championship.
First prediction of the year nailed.
Would’ve preferred that one took a week to develop.
The good news is Lamar and Hurts are still awesome.
Lamar: 26.96.
Hurts: 30.72.
The bad news is apparently they need to be.
DeVonta Smith: 6.8.
Jameson Williams: 6.5.
DK Metcalf: 6.
Marvin Harrison Jr.: 3.8.
My four starting receivers combined for 23.1 points.
Hurts outscored all four by himself.
Stefon Diggs was the only receiver on the roster who remembered touchdowns count. DeVonta at least recovered Washington’s onside kick to help the actual Eagles win.
Huge play. Very clutch. Go Birds 🦅
Sleeper awarded me zero points for leadership.
DK got ten targets and turned them into 40 yards. Jamo had 45. Marvin Harrison caught one pass.
That one was especially fun.
I traded Derrick Henry for Marvin because I wanted to get younger.
Henry opened the season with 144 yards and three touchdowns.
Marvin caught one football for 33 yards.
Dynasty.
Very sophisticated stuff.

The running back room is also going exactly according to plan. Josh Jacobs is unavailable. Kamara was out. Kyren Williams and 31-year-old Aaron Jones are currently standing between me and meaningful Will Shipley snaps.
Meanwhile Tyler Shough threw for 410 yards and three touchdowns.
The most encouraging young player on my team is my 27-year-old QB3.
Perfect.
I scored 128.58 anyway, which is probably the only reason I’m not joining Mike and putting half the roster on the trade block after one Sunday.
Darren has been predicting the death of the Delco Dreamers for what feels like my entire adult life. After Week 1, he finally has some decent material.
He can wait.
And yes, Brian is 1-0.
I am 0-1.
I am still ranking myself ahead of him.
I do the power rankings around here.
2: Jalen Royals was Joe’s last player Monday night.
Kansas City scored 31 points. Kenneth Walker ran for 173 yards and two touchdowns. Mahomes threw two touchdowns and ran for another.
Royals scored 0.00.
Connecticut finished Week 1 with 15 points.
An absolute tanking masterclass.
Five starters gave Joe a zero. Mason Taylor caught two passes for negative two yards and still outscored all five of them.
I also owe Joe a correction from the preseason rankings. He owns eight 2027 firsts, not nine.
How embarrassing for him.
Only two-thirds of the first round.
I’m not convinced Sunday was even the most important football day of Joe’s weekend.
Jeremiah Smith went for 164 yards and a touchdown against Texas. Arch Manning helped bring Texas back from 23-3 down in the fourth quarter to beat No. 1 Ohio State 24-23.
Joe probably enjoyed Saturday just fine.
That’s basically his season now. Every Saturday, some 2027-eligible player is going to do something stupid and immediately become relevant to Connecticut.

Smith is the obvious prize. He’s also not going to be the only guy everyone wants by April. Somebody is going to come out of nowhere. Some running back is going to have a ridiculous October. A quarterback nobody cares about right now is going to end up in first-round mocks.
Joe gets eight swings.
Meanwhile his actual fantasy team can put up 15 points and it barely matters.
Honestly, kind of peaceful.
There may be one current Croc who suddenly has some value, though.
Keenan Allen.
Jeff lost A.J. Brown to a high-ankle sprain and now AJB is on IR. Zay Flowers got banged up too.
Joe has an old receiver he absolutely does not need.
Jeff spent the entire offseason trading like Sleeper was shutting down forever at midnight.
You see where this is going.
Maybe Jeff finally discovers restraint.
No.
I don’t believe that either.
I’m calling it now: Keenan Allen ends up in Wichita.
I have no idea what Jeff gives up. Probably something I’ll hate. Joe will probably somehow turn a 34-year-old receiver into another pick and make this whole thing even more annoying.
For now, though:
Five goose eggs.
Fifteen total points.
Eight 2027 firsts.
Joe is 0-1 and probably having more fun than half the league.
3: We nearly talked ourselves into picking Welch over Jeff on the podcast.

Everyone had Wichita except Welch, then Darren started looking at the Week 1 matchups and almost flipped. Mahomes coming back from the knee against Denver. McCaffrey in that weird Australia game. A.J. Brown against Seattle.
By Monday night, Welch may have even felt somewhat comfortable with his lead heading into the Denver vs KC game.
Bad plan.
Jeff had Mahomes, Kenneth Walker and Travis Kelce going Monday night.
They combined for 67.36 points.
Nearly half of Wichita’s entire score came from one NFL offense.

Walker was the killer. First game with Kansas City, 173 rushing yards and two touchdowns, including a 60-yarder. Mahomes added two passing touchdowns and ran for another in his first game back from the knee injury. Kelce had 71 yards and casually passed Jason Witten for second all-time in receiving yards by a tight end.
Jeff spent the offseason collecting stars and apparently finished by just buying the Chiefs.
A handful of 2027 fourths for Kelce also looked considerably less stupid when he immediately gave Jeff 10 points while making NFL history.
Wichita beat Dallas 142.42 to 128.76, and the funniest part is Jeff’s ridiculous offseason shopping spree already gave him a reason to start shopping again.
A.J. Brown gave him 4.1, suffered a high ankle sprain and is now on IR. He has to miss at least four games, with the current expectation closer to six weeks.
Zay Flowers was awesome, 150 yards and a touchdown before his hamstring decided that was enough football for one afternoon.
So Jeff’s starting receivers produced one huge game, two 4.1s, one trip to IR and one hamstring injury.

Samuel and Jakobi Meyers at least gave him usable games on the bench, but I already said it in Joe’s section: Keenan Allen is sitting on a rebuilding roster in Connecticut and Jeff suddenly needs a receiver.
The other thing I wanted to see was whether this team actually felt as ridiculous once all the names were in one lineup. It did.
Mahomes. Burrow. McCaffrey. Saquon. Kenneth Walker. A.J. Brown. Davante. Flowers. Kelce.
This looks like somebody turned the salary cap off on Madden (has anyone played the latest Madden? Is it good?)
And even with McCaffrey and Saquon combining for less than 20, A.J. getting hurt and Davante doing basically nothing, Wichita still put up 142.
Jeff spent years rebuilding at the bottom of these rankings.
Now he gets one week into the season, and his biggest concern is figuring out which contender-level receiver he wants to buy next.
Disgusting.
4: Max spent the entire offseason telling us nobody believed in Murphy Street Empire.

Darren said the roster wasn’t that great. Max took it personally. Every MSE conversation eventually became some version of the same argument: everyone is sleeping on this team, everyone is disrespecting what’s still here, everyone is acting like one of the PDL’s original powers suddenly became some fringe roster overnight.
Week 1 ends.
Chase Brown is already on the trade block.
Uh oh.
We were trying to believe longer than you did.
At least we didn’t make MSE-Boulder our actual Game of the Week. Tanish won by 45.48 and put up the highest score in the league.
Max also spent part of the offseason defending Tanish and saying everyone was just jealous of him.
Tanish thanked him by beating the shit out of him.
There were good things here. Jalen Coker nearly dropped 30. Dak was fine. Ladd scored. Coker having that kind of Week 1 is exactly the type of thing Max needed from the middle of this roster.
Then Coker showed up in a walking boot.
Of course.

And now Chase Brown is apparently available after one bad week, which I especially enjoy because Darren literally described him during the preseason rankings as one of those players “only Max really likes.”
Apparently Max’s membership has been revoked.
The bigger issue might be Tennessee.

Cam Ward and Carnell Tate were supposed to be the new thing Max could point to while the old MSE core aged out. Young quarterback. Fourth-overall receiver. Stack them together and let the next version of Murphy Street grow around them.
Ward looked rough throughout August.
The pocket awareness was strange. The mechanics fell apart when pressure showed up. Every time any of us mentioned it, the answer was the same one everyone gives in August.
It’s preseason.
Doesn’t matter.
Then Tennessee played a game that counted.
195 total yards.
Longest play: 14 yards.
Ward threw for 140, took three sacks, got pressured on 41% of his dropbacks, and Titans fans were already chanting “Fire Saleh” before Robert Saleh had even completed his first game as head coach.
Maybe preseason counts a little.
Tate finished with four catches for 38 yards.
Nothing is decided after one game, obviously. Ward and Tate could look completely different by October. Max doesn’t need either of them to become a superstar next Sunday.
He does need Tennessee to occasionally resemble an NFL offense.
That stack matters too much to what comes next for MSE for the Titans to spend Sundays generating 14-yard explosives.
The other thing hanging over all of this is that Max spent August arguing that we were discounting him while quietly doing some things that looked an awful lot like a guy hedging his bets.

Travis Kelce went to Wichita for three fourths right before the season. Greg and Darren both asked the obvious question on the podcast: if Max really thinks this team can make the playoffs, why move a tight end he would actually use for a handful of future fourths?
Now Chase Brown is on the block.
One week.
I’m not saying Max is blowing it up. I don’t think he is.
But “nobody believes in my team” lands a little differently when we’re apparently accepting offers.
And I’m still in.

Ja’Marr is still one of the best players in fantasy. Ladd is great. Coker just reminded everyone why people liked him. Stroud put 20 on the bench. Monangai had a big week down there too. There is enough talent here that Max could win next week and immediately return to the chat demanding apologies from all of us.
That would actually be very Max.

But the old MSE could absorb bad news almost indefinitely. Somebody got hurt, somebody disappointed, Max made a terrible start/sit call, whatever. There was always another good player hiding somewhere.
That cushion is thinner now.
Week 1 made it obvious.
I’m still buying Murphy Street more than Max apparently is.
He should probably take Chase Brown off the trade block before I change my mind.
5: Jon spent all offseason waiting to finally see the rookie class he bought into.
By Sunday afternoon, he probably wanted another preseason game.
Richmond scored 56.9, which sounds considerably better once you remember Joe scored 15.
Nearly quadrupled him.
Hang the banner.
Fernando Mendoza never got off the bench, although nobody expected him to. The No. 1 pick became the first first-overall quarterback since Baker Mayfield in 2018 to not start Week 1.
Kirk Cousins then threw three touchdowns in a Raiders win.
Great news for Las Vegas.
Slightly less exciting for the guy waiting for Nando.
Makai Lemon finally returned after spending most of the offseason dealing with his hamstring.
Three catches.
Negative five yards.
3 for -5.
As an Eagles fan, I watched enough of it to confirm the box score somehow made it look better.
Lemon has now been targeted nine times between the preseason and Week 1 and those targets have produced negative yardage.
We’re off and running.

Jordyn Tyson, probably the rookie Jon was most excited to see because he’s apparently a Saints fan, is still waiting. The eighth overall pick remains out with the hamstring injury expected to cost him roughly two months.
Then Omar Cooper caught a 30-yard pass on his first target.
Broke a couple tackles.
Took the Jets down near the goal line.
High ankle sprain.
Same play.
Jesus Christ.
Kenyon Sadiq was the one rookie who actually let Jon enjoy himself for a few minutes. The Jets handed him the ball on their opening drive and he scored the first touchdown of their season.
11.4 points for Richmond.
Antonio Williams added 14.4, so Jon at least got a couple signs of life before checking the injury report again.
This season was always going to be ugly. Jon knew that when he tore Michael’s old roster apart.
He just probably pictured the young guys making the ugly part more entertaining.
Week 1 gave him a backup quarterback, negative receiving yards, one hamstring rehab, one high ankle sprain and a Kenyon Sadiq touchdown.
Welcome to the rebuild.
6: Brian is 1-0.
I am 0-1.
SPOILER ALERT: I am ranking myself ahead of him.
Delco scored 128.58 and lost. Hollywood scored 121.48 against Jon, who put up 56.9.
The committee has reviewed the matter and found no wrongdoing.
Moving on.
Darren planted his flag before Week 1 that Hollywood was making the playoffs. We made him stop hedging and actually say it. Brian will make the playoffs.
Then Hollywood opens against Richmond.
Really putting your neck out there, Darren.

Still, Brian got exactly what he needed out of Week 1. Parker Washington spent the entire summer generating the type of training-camp headlines dynasty owners use to annoy their friends, then actually backed it up with 83 yards and a touchdown in Jacksonville’s 34-10 win.
Five catches. 83 yards. Score.
Fine, Brian. You can keep talking about him.

Jeremiyah Love scored on the third carry of his NFL career too, which is especially annoying after Darren spent the preseason comparing his running style to Adrian Peterson and everybody immediately started yelling at him to clarify what exactly he meant.
Three carries.
Touchdown.
I’ve now seen enough other people make the AD comparison that I’m becoming concerned Darren may have actually watched football.
Hollywood also has Jordan Love, so Brian currently employs two different Loves.
Excellent timing considering we spent part of the Week 1 podcast discussing Daejon Love, the fake 49ers player accused of scamming at least 26 women out of roughly $1.3 million.
One of the aliases federal authorities say he used?
Jordan Love.
I checked Brian’s roster.
His Jordan Love appears to be the real one.
Jeremiyah too.
Good to verify these things now.

The legitimate Jordan Love threw for 387 yards and two touchdowns Sunday, then watched Green Bay blow a 22-10 lead while Carson Wentz came off Minnesota’s bench and led four straight touchdown drives. The Vikings scored the final 29 points.
Carson Wentz doing this to the Packers in 2026 is what Welch gets for refusing to say “Go Birds” in the chat.
Brian doesn’t care. Twenty-two fantasy points count the same whether Green Bay leaves the stadium happy or needs grief counseling.
Hollywood didn’t need one guy to go completely insane either. Nico scored. Washington delivered. Both Loves contributed. Malik Willis gave him a useful week. Egbuka was involved.
That’s a better sign for Brian than somebody randomly dropping 40 and covering up a bad lineup.
I had Hollywood ninth because once you got through the names at the top, I thought this roster got sketchy pretty quickly.
One week in and Parker Washington is making me revisit that. Jeremiyah Love immediately looks useful. There were actual options on the bench.
Great.
Another offseason take aging beautifully.
Brian did beat Jon, so I’m not handing Darren his playoff-prediction trophy yet. Everyone should beat Jon this year. If you lose to Richmond, I’m probably dropping you three spots on principle.
But Brian is already 1-0, Darren has his first receipt, and I own Hollywood’s 2027 first.
So naturally the best possible outcome for me is Brian turning out to be much better than I thought.
Excellent asset management.
Hollywood wins.
Hollywood moves up.
Hollywood is still behind my winless team.
Feel free to file a complaint directly with the commissioner.
7: Darren spent the preseason rankings telling us exactly where the problem was.
“Quarterback. My quarterback room is, I would say, my weakness.”
Matthew Stafford went all the way to Australia to score Darren 3.1 points.
The Rams showed up in Melbourne barely a day before kickoff, got smoked 27-7, and Stafford finished with 155 yards and a pick.
Probably should’ve stayed on Murican time.
Baker Mayfield wasn’t exactly comforting either. He lost three fumbles against Cincinnati, including one at the goal line. Tampa turned it over four times total.

And then Brock Bowers, arguably the biggest positional advantage on this entire roster, randomly underwent a meniscus trim and got ruled out right before the season. The injury wasn’t even public until Wednesday.
Good thing Darren has approximately 14 tight ends.
Kittle gave him 3.2, though, so the big TE premium advantage was essentially closed for renovations this week.
None of it mattered because Darren played Joe.

Gibbs looked ridiculous. Javonte scored twice. CeeDee, Garrett Wilson, Mike Evans, Etienne, everyone gave him enough. And because Darren’s roster is incredibly deep, D’Andre Swift put up 31.9 on the bench while DJ Moore had 18.5.
So the Thunder survived Week 1 with their biggest weakness looking exactly like their biggest weakness and their best tight end unavailable.
Against Connecticut, you can get away with that.
The next time Stafford gives Darren three points, he should probably hope the opponent also starts five guys who score zero.
8: I had the Breece Hall paragraph written in my head by halftime.

Welch finally makes one aggressive trade after years of treating every offer like it came from a Nigerian prince, sends Breece to Greg for two seconds, and Breece immediately opens the season with 102 yards and a touchdown.
Easy.
Except Dallas got 44.2 points from Bucky Irving and David Montgomery.
So unfortunately I have to be fair.
The Breece trade was not why Welch lost.
This was much funnier.
Kyler Murray gave him -1.38 before leaving Minnesota’s opener with a concussion. Carson Wentz came in, the Vikings scored 29 straight points, and Minnesota somehow beat Green Bay 39-22.
Welch is a Vikings fan.
Christian Watson plays for Green Bay.
Christian Watson is also on Welch’s bench.
He caught six balls for 147 yards and two touchdowns.
29.7 fantasy points.

So Welch got to spend Sunday watching his starting fantasy quarterback leave after scoring negative points, his backup real-life quarterback Carson Wentz become a Vikings hero, and one of the best players on his fantasy bench torch the Vikings while doing absolutely nothing for Dallas.
That is an incredible way to experience one football game.
Bryce Young also scored 36.44 on the bench, because apparently Welch’s QB room operates on a strict “everyone except the starter” policy.
And Dallas still scored 128.76.

Amon-Ra had two touchdowns. McBride gave him 24.5. Montgomery went for 27.4. Even with Drake London and Terry McLaurin combining for less than seven points, Welch was hanging around against Jeff’s newly assembled Death Star.
He lost by 13.66.

Honestly, after all the shit we gave him for moving Breece, Week 1 probably strengthened Welch’s argument more than ours. His running backs were great without him. The roster survived a negative score at quarterback. Christian Watson sat there with almost 30 unused points and Dallas still made Wichita work for it.
Two seconds, Welch.
Two.
But after Week 1, Dallas looks less like the team that made a stupid trade and more like the team that might survive one.
Which is considerably less funny.
9: Greg spent the offseason talking about the return of the run game, 13 personnel, and why everybody was too scared to build around running backs.
The King looks to continue his reign. 144 yards, three touchdowns, moved into third all-time in rushing touchdowns, and did it against the Colts while Greg was beating me by 18.
Really enjoying the Marvin Harrison trade so far.

Breece went over 100 and scored in the Jets win, Bijan gave him another 90 rushing and a touchdown, and suddenly the roster Greg spent two years tearing down looks exactly like the stupid thing he kept promising it would become.
Then Chris Olave went for 10 catches and 182 yards, the best receiving total in the NFL in Week 1.
Great. Maybe Mike will finally give me Rome.

The whole league knows Greg has been trying to acquire Rome Odunze for roughly two years. Saying he’s “been interested” doesn’t really cover it. I genuinely don’t know if 80 offers is an exaggeration.
Monday, Greg finally sends him to Mike with a 2028 fourth and gets Rome and Courtland Sutton back.
Rome himself had two catches for 52 yards in Chicago’s 59-point explosion, including a 47-yarder that helped set up a touchdown.
I don’t think Greg cared what Rome did Sunday. At some point this stopped being roster construction and became a personal mission.
10: Tanish scored the most points in the league.
He is the defending champion.
And I’m still putting Mike first.
Sorry, Tanish.
Mike scored 158.26, one point behind Boulder, and somehow there was still plenty for him to be annoyed about. Achane gave him 8.6. Puka 9.9. Pickens 4.3. Waddle gave him 0.7.
This is exactly the kind of Sunday where Mike scores 158 and still opens the app Monday morning staring angrily at four players.

Josh Allen gave him 39.66 after throwing for 334 yards and accounting for four touchdowns in Buffalo’s comeback win over Houston. Ashton Jeanty, who Mike spent half the summer worrying about, went for 147 total yards and two touchdowns. Justin Jefferson scored twice.
All offseason there was some new reason for Mike to worry about this roster. Jeanty’s health. Puka. Rome. Achane. Something was always about to go wrong.
Jeanty finally plays and immediately drops 29.7.
Mike survived.
And then Greg decided the best team in the league needed help.
Chris Olave had 10 catches for 182 yards in Week 1.
Naturally, about 24 hours later, Greg traded him to Southern Oregon for Rome Odunze and Courtland Sutton.
Thanks, Greg.
The team that already had Josh Allen, Jeanty, Achane, Puka, Justin Jefferson, Waddle and Pickens now gets the guy who just led Week 1 with 182 receiving yards.
Mike even got a fourth back.
Very necessary.

Meanwhile, Isaiah Likely scored 27.8 on his bench, Evan Engram had 14.3, and there are still enough useful players down there that Mike can continue his annual tradition of having six guys on the trade block after one bad Sunday and then rejecting every offer he receives.
Except now I’m not sure what the bad Sunday is supposed to look like.
He scored 158 with four starters under ten.
Then upgraded at receiver.
I had Southern Oregon first in the preseason because I thought it was the best roster in the league.
One week later, Tanish did everything possible to take the spot from him.
Greg made sure he didn’t.
11: Last week I accidentally ranked Dubrovnik 10th instead of 9th.
I corrected it. Made a whole thing out of fixing it.
I would like the typo back.
The Dragons spent Week 1 doing a pretty convincing Delco impression. Both quarterbacks went nuclear while everyone else mostly stood around.
Jaxson Dart: 32.6.
Trevor Lawrence: 34.1.
That’s 66.7 points from two players.
Dubrovnik finished with 111.2.
You can do the subtraction yourself.
Dart also deserves an apology from me because six days earlier I spent an unreasonable amount of the podcast explaining why I didn’t trust the Giants offense.
Matt Nagy. The offensive line. Nabers coming back. The division. Dart constantly trying to get himself killed.
I think at one point I had seven different reasons.
Apparently I forgot one important detail.
They were playing the Dallas defense.
Three passing touchdowns, 54 rushing yards, Giants win.
Great start for me.

Trevor Lawrence was even better. Four touchdowns in a 34-10 Jacksonville win, and suddenly Brett has two quarterbacks that looked exactly like the reason some psychopath ranked Dubrovnik sixth in the preseason.
The rest of the lineup was considerably less inspiring.
Omarion Hampton gave him 8.3 against Arizona, which is not exactly what you were hoping for.
Tet had 8.
Dobbins had 3.6.
And then there was Colston Loveland.
Chicago scored 59 points.
Carolina scored 37.
Ninety-six total points were scored in that football game.
Loveland gave Brett 0.00.
That takes effort.
Tucker Kraft at least gave him 9.5, so the great young Dubrovnik tight end room technically participated in Week 1. Just not the one we spent all offseason getting excited about.
None of this is really a disaster for Brett because he has told us approximately 400 times that he isn’t trying to compete this year.
He backed that up again right before kickoff by sending Jaden Reed back to Greg for my 2027 second and a 2028 third.
Apparently Brett also told Greg during negotiations that my second is going to be 2.01.
Fuck you too, Brett.
He’s at least consistent.
Carnell Tate gone.
Jaden Reed gone.
Keep pushing things into the future. Let Dart, Hampton, Tet, Loveland and the rest of the young guys develop. Really start trying next year.
Sure.
The problem is Dart and Lawrence apparently didn’t get the memo.
Because this is how the whole “we’re competing next year” thing gets messy.
Your quarterbacks start dropping 30.
Some of the young guys hit faster than expected.
You accidentally win a few games.
Then it’s October and you’re sitting there wondering why Carnell Tate is on somebody else’s roster because he was apparently too young for the rebuild.
I still don’t understand that trade.
I promised myself I wouldn’t bring it up every week.
No such promise was made about the Jaden Reed trade.
So yes, Brett, I’m sorry I ranked you 10th by accident last week.
After Week 1, I should have trusted my instincts.
Or my inability to use a spreadsheet.
Either way.
#10 Dubrovnik Dragons.
12: Tanish won the championship.
Spent the entire offseason listening to us explain why it was lucky.
Then opened the new season by scoring 159.28, more than anybody else in the league.
So naturally I have him ranked third.
I understand how this looks.
Boulder beat Max by 45.48 and did it without even needing much from Drake Maye, who gave Tanish 8.82 while throwing three interceptions against Seattle.
Tanish is still "stuck" with his great trio of QBs so he's fine.
Jayden Daniels put up 21.66 on the bench.
For roughly two years we’ve been telling Tanish he should trade one of these quarterbacks.
He has instead chosen the much simpler strategy of owning all of them.
Working so far.
And unlike last year’s playoff run, there wasn’t anything particularly weird about this one.
Jonathan Taylor: 23.6.
Kincaid: 18.
Rhamondre: 12.
Even Chuba Hubbard dropped 22.2 on the bench.
No Samaje Perine playoff sorcery. No Mack Hollins emergency start. Just a really good fantasy team beating the shit out of Max.
Which is particularly funny because Max was one of the only people defending Tanish all offseason.
Everyone else kept calling the championship lucky. Max kept telling us to give the man some respect.
Tanish now has exactly what he wanted.
Receipts.
Every time somebody calls last year a fluke, he can just point at the trophy and then point at Week 1.
And I still can’t put him first.
Mike’s roster is disgusting. I picked Greggy to win.
Sorry, Tanish.
Defending champion.
Highest score in Week 1.
Still #3.
At some point, this probably stops being disrespect and starts becoming a personal issue.
